column1: # What enforces each requirement in this repository's specs (0020-spec-format FR-011 – FR-014).
# mechanism: check | gate | review | none. by: "<repo>: <command>" for check and gate, the defining requirement for review, "-" for none.

column4: note
scope
doctor reports the runtime's Python and the distribution; tests run the install in fresh Debian and Ubuntu containers
tests run the launcher from another directory, through absolute and relative links, bootstrap the runtime into an empty store, verify the pinned checksum, and refuse offline
a test reads pyproject.toml and the presence of uv.lock; the core's imports are parsed
tests run install.sh against a local remote: clone, link, doctor, a repeat, a clone with edits, a missing prerequisite
the install tests use WS_HOST_URL and WS_HOST_HOME
tests run in a temporary HOME and read the paths from the XDG variables
tests parse the configuration, refuse a secrets file others can read, and keep secrets out of doctor and context
WORKSPACES_HOME is exported when programs are run, which arrives with the commands that run them
finds conflicts and module-level third-party imports; tests cover both
tests run every command that takes no required argument in three renderings
tests run doctor against a malformed configuration, a loose secrets file and a registry conflict
tests run the sections, an unknown section, and a section that could not run
test is itself the runner; its result fails when no test ran
tests check the first line of text renderings and that actions print as one line or not at all
tests check what is logged, with its surface, and that a read is not

tests check by reading the source that every check which can warn or fail carries an action, a line or what to do, that a finding with none gets a plain line asking for help, the fixes of a loose secrets file, a bad configuration, a missing launcher, an unset pull setting and a waiting update, and that the sentence says nothing of below

tests check the title and icon of every command, the ellipsis rule, the views, nouns and lists, that the rows of each list carry the fields it names and a status that maps, the pinned icons against the public root's, each mistake FR-072 names failing check registry, and .workspaces-host/provider.toml
a test reads every tracked file for the name of a confidential repository and what it holds; the history is not checked
the listing tests resolve full, short and ambiguous names
tests read the person's list and a cloned repository's file, to any depth, ignore a malformed entry, and need no trust
tests run repo list and repo status against real clones: ahead, behind, dirty, branch
tests clone into the layout, trust nothing, and take --dry-run
tests run a failed clone, a clone of a private repository without sign-in (git's own reason and the auth action), and one failure among several
tests clone a repository only another's file names and leave it untrusted
tests spy on every git call: no pull, rebase, stash, reset or checkout, and merge only with --ff-only
tests leave dirty, diverged, no-upstream, detached, mid-rebase and unpushed-conflicting repositories exactly as they were (HEAD, index, status, no stash, no rebase or merge state) with exit 0
tests read the plain-language reason of each skip and the note on unpushed work
tests read each outcome: updated with a count, current, skipped, failed
tests run auth status and auth new against a fake gh and glab: signed in or out, the streamed code and address, a failed login, a missing program (exit 3)
tests grant and revoke trust through the relative link, an organization in the person's configuration, and a name collision
tests list a repository named by a trusted one as untrusted and ignore a repository's own WS_HOST_TRUSTED, with doctor saying so
tests confirm a decision only from a terminal answer or the editor's confirmation, refuse it otherwise, keep it off MCP, and list what --trust trusts
tests record the commit and make doctor warn, not fail, when a trusted repository's kits changed
tests run workspace ensure end to end: steps, a repeat that changes nothing, past a failure, dry run, status
tests check doctor recommends pull.ff only, never applies it, and workspace set applies it on request
tests check a clone's ignored and untracked state and the person's git configuration after repo sync
tests run kit list, show and an unknown kit, and that actions print as one line
tests check kit add is setup and cli only, says it will use sudo before running, uses sudo -n without a terminal and says what to run when refused
tests resolve a|b names and report a package the distribution lacks without stopping the install
tests and the container runs end with the kit's programs, versions and functional checks
tests run the package installer against a stand-in apt-get, installing only what is missing, as root without sudo
tests run the download installer with real archives: verification, a wrong checksum, atomic current, links, a repeat, an older version kept, a failed step, unsafe paths
tests check --dry-run and --offline fetch and install nothing and exit 3 naming the download
tests check base's programs and the userland, WebP and Chromium checks; the container runs on Debian and Ubuntu
tests check press's packages; the container runs the lualatex check on Debian and Ubuntu
tests check rust's version and download; the container runs the rustc check and a cargo build of a reqwest and rustls crate
tests check every download's checksum form, address template and architecture
tests run workspace ensure over declared kits (see 0002 FR-016); a declared kit that is unknown is reported
tests check doctor says a trusted repository's kits are not loaded yet
retired: ws-host ships no extension; the Workspaces Console is the one extension (0009-workspaces-console FR-001, FR-002).
retired: the Workspaces Console discovers launchers by their own declaration and holds no rule of any orchestrator (0009-workspaces-console FR-003 to FR-005).
retired: the Workspaces Console runs only in a trusted workspace for a trusted repository (0009-workspaces-console FR-006).
retired: the Workspaces Console's status bar item names how many things need a person and what to do (0009-workspaces-console FR-016, FR-048).
retired: the Workspaces Console's views and tree come from the command line's own presentation (0009-workspaces-console FR-008, FR-036; 0001-ws-host FR-018).
retired: the Workspaces Console draws a resource in one panel from its JSON (0009-workspaces-console FR-003, FR-042).
retired: the Workspaces Console builds the input of a command from its typed arguments (0009-workspaces-console FR-013).
retired: the Workspaces Console follows a stream as progress (0009-workspaces-console FR-020).
retired: the Workspaces Console shows the findings of a check in the Problems panel (0009-workspaces-console FR-009).
retired: the Workspaces Console checks each document's schema (0009-workspaces-console FR-021).
retired: a decision needs a modal and no command takes an action (0009-workspaces-console FR-015).
retired: the Workspaces Console writes nothing itself (0009-workspaces-console FR-026).
retired: what a command logs names its surface (0041-command-line FR-042).
retired: signing in is an action like any other (0009-workspaces-console FR-013 to FR-015); the sign-in code is shown by the resource `auth new` returns.
retired: the Workspaces Console offers Get Help and Copy Context (0009-workspaces-console FR-012, FR-018).
retired: `vscode ensure` installs the Workspaces Console from the public root (FR-021).
retired: the contract the Workspaces Console relies on is tested from Python (FR-025).

tests check the recommended set and baseline and that the generated reference lists them
tests check the WSL machine settings path, a commented file left alone with the values listed, and the backup
a test reads pages.yml for the Pages actions, main, the tests and fresh before the build, and the maintainer note on the one setting; the deploy itself runs on GitHub
tests build the site with a stand-in asciidoctor: a page per chapter with navigation and a pager, cross-references resolved; the container builds it with the real one
tests check the chapters exist in the required order and each start page says where to type
tests check every blocker the spec names is a symptom with a cause and a fix
tests check the vendor links are https and present
a test checks the README is five steps and links the site
tests check no escape codes or emoji off a terminal, bold and marks and a coloured command on one, NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb and WS_HOST_COLOR, and none in JSON or HTML
tests check the start page's sections, their order, and the lines to type, with and without colour, and that install.sh ends by showing it
tests check the starter repositories, an explicit list and an empty one, and cloning them into the layout
tests check repo add puts a new address on the person's list, keeps their other lines and the starters, copies it, and changes nothing in a dry run

tests check install.sh ends with the one line to start a new login shell when ~/.local/bin was not on the PATH and says nothing when it was, and that uv's installer is told not to edit shell files

tests check the default kits are base and shell, the prompt given to bash by workspace ensure and not in a dry run or with WS_HOST_PROMPT=no, never failing setup, that setup leaves an existing prompt block alone, and that ws-host-plain holds no private-use font glyph while both themes print a prompt

tests run the generated bash script on every command, noun, verb, option and kit, the fish script where fish is installed, the dynamic repository values at Tab time, the written files, a person's own file left alone, a second run changing nothing, and that no startup file is edited

tests check the sections, marks, counts, wrapping within the terminal's width, long names, fixes and next steps in cyan for doctor, kits, repositories and commands, that the first line is the plain sentence, and that a pipe, JSON and HTML are not decorated

tests use a local remote to check update --check and update (news listed, forward only, changes of the person's, diverged and ahead copies and an unreachable remote left alone), the note, the doctor row, the six-hour rule, and the bash block run in a shell with a stand-in ws-host

tests check the tarball holds the wheel package, a launcher and nothing else, and runs through a symbolic link; check release runs the built one
tests check the tarball and a rewritten zip are the same bytes whatever the time; check reproducible builds again and compares every byte

a test checks a dry run builds nothing and names the files; release build refuses differing versions
tests check each finding of the release section, that a tampered file ends it at the checksums and that a leaking package fails

tests check archive platforms, checksums, strip, bin, provides, env, needs and system are read
tests check npm and tool entries need their own key
tests check each rejection names the file and the key
tests check the translation is deterministic, generated files say so, stale files are named and fixed, and the providers section fails on them
tests check an install uses only the translation, in one store, and reads no configuration above the provider
tests check the pinned mise per architecture, and WS_HOST_MISE as the only override
tests check two providers declaring one name and version differently conflict, and provider add refuses
tests check nothing is enabled without a person's decision, add links and remove unlinks
tests check provider list and show say each provider, entry and state
tests check ensure installs from the lock, toolchain show reports state and path, and a stale translation stops it
tests check provider run puts the entries first on PATH, passes the exit status and puts nothing on a person's PATH
ws-host passes through the person's variables and mise's own; the provider removes the rest (see 0008-providers FR-013)
tests check toolchain remove --unused removes only what no provider's lock names and --dry-run writes nothing
tests check system ensure with and without libraries, and its dry run
tests check doctor reports each provider and brew and direnv as suggestions
the manifest is read: id, display name, prefixes, no API export
the lint refuses another repository's or orchestrator's name in console/; public-only is otherwise a review

discovery tests: declaration, rejected names, person-only setting
handshake tests with a fake and the real launcher
trust tests: nothing runs untrusted; the reason and the trust action are shown
tests with two folders whose launchers share a name
tree tests: nouns, commands, resources, links, actions, disabled with reason
diagnostics tests: file:line, severity, source, cleared per section, unplaced findings in the output
task provider and Test Controller tests; a skipped section is skipped, never passed
webview tests: policy, link classification, one own script, local resources only, no --html asked for

tests: modal required, exactly true, forged nodes ignored, no API export, no decision in the manifest's tasks or keys

tests: a newer schema is not shown and an update is offered

no check; installation is a person's act

language tests for the hover, definition, CodeLens and document links from the references' own patterns and show; the real VS Code run drives them in a fixture and in this repository's register
